chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Bukayr ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Aba Ja'far عليه السلام about wudu (ablution) from that which the fire has changed, so he said: “There is no wudu upon you concerning it. Wudu is only from that which exits, not from that which enters.”

key_terms.النَّارُ: fire, meaning food cooked or heated by fire
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification discussed in the ruling
key_terms.غَيَّرَتِ: changed or altered, referring to food affected by fire
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ: there is no obligation upon you
key_terms.يَخْرُجُ: what exits, referring to substances that invalidate wudu
key_terms.يَدْخُلُ: what enters, referring to food or drink that does not invalidate wudu

ai.seo_question: Does eating cooked food invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that consuming food altered by fire does not require wudu (ablution). It clarifies that what invalidates wudu is what exits the body, not what enters it.
